_meta.method: Web search plus direct fetches of publisher pages; PDFs were read with pdftotext. Where a publisher page would not render (ba.com sat behind a queue page; aeromexico.com and vuela.aeromexico.com showed a maintenance error; Ryanair's help pages are a single-page app), the figure comes from secondary reporting or the search index and is marked confirmed:false.
_meta.conventions: sourceType 'primary' = statute, regulator, or the company's own page or terms; 'secondary' = press, a broker aggregating others, a blog, or a marketplace listing written by the owner. confirmed:true = the figure was read on the cited page during this session. null = not published or not found; the note says which.
_meta.spelling: American spelling in our own words; quoted text keeps the source's spelling.

nationalFloor.text: Loss Damage Waiver (LDW) as low as $9/day

waiverPricesAtCounters.note: Avis publishes only a national 'as low as $9/day' figure, with no price per location. In New York the statute caps it by vehicle value anyway (see nyCap below). Secondary sources give a $9 to $35.99 range, which is not confirmed.
Enterprise shows no price for any US location outside the booking flow. For compact through full-size cars, California caps it at $25/day adjusted by CPI from 2023 (see caCap).
Not published. Connecticut has no statutory cap that we found.

The Enterprise Canada FAQ says the cost 'can vary based on the type of vehicle'. It gives no amount. A search snippet cited 'between $9.99 and $39.99 CAD per day' as coming from Enterprise's Canadian site, but that text was not on the page when fetched.
Not published. The same Canada-wide FAQ applies.

nyCap.law: New York General Business Law §396-z (rental vehicle protections)

renterLiability.damage: The renter's liability is capped at the lesser of the actual repair cost (after the company's discounts) or the car's fair market value just before the damage.
renterLiability.theft: The renter is liable only if the driver failed to take reasonable care or helped with the theft. Liability is then capped at the company's reasonable costs, up to fair market value.
renterLiability.lossOfUseAndAdminFees: Not recoverable from an authorized driver or the driver's insurer.
renterLiability.doubleRecovery: The company can't bill the renter for amounts it recovers from another party.

nyCap.pending: Bill S3246B (2025–26) would index the $9/$12/$15 caps to CPI-U from January 1, 2027 and remove the 2028 sunset. It was amended and recommitted to the Consumer Protection committee on 2026-01-14 and has not passed. Some secondary sites print $12/$15 with a $30,000 threshold, but that is not current law.

caCap.law: California Civil Code §1939.09(d), as amended by AB 901 (Stats. 2021, ch. 415), effective 2022-01-01

dailyCap.appliesTo: the five smallest ACRISS body-size categories: economy, compact, intermediate, standard and full-size

caCap.indexation: Adjusted upward each year from January 1, 2023 by the CPI-U. We did not find a published indexed figure for 2026.
caCap.otherCategories: The fetched text sets no cap for larger categories.
caCap.wasNine: No. $9/day was an older California cap and also New York's lowest tier. The current California figure is $25 plus CPI.
caCap.waiverScope: A damage waiver relieves the renter of liability for damage, loss, loss of use and related costs. The statute declares any limitation, exception or exclusion to the waiver void.

maxRecoverable: Collision damage, up to the car's fair market value, regardless of cause

Theft, up to fair market value, only if the company proves by clear and convincing evidence that the driver failed to take ordinary care. The renter is presumed not liable if the driver returns the key and files a police report within 24 hours.
Vandalism connected with a theft, up to fair market value
Vandalism unrelated to a theft: capped at $500
Actual towing, storage and impound fees
An administrative charge that covers appraisal and other incidental costs. The fetched text gave no amount cap.
renterLiabilityWithoutWaiver_1939_03.lossOfUse: Not in the list of recoverable items in the fetched text.

avis.text: If you decline both LDW and PDW, "you owe for all loss or damage to the car."

enterpriseContractTerms.repair: The repair estimate, or fair market value if the car is a total loss
enterpriseContractTerms.lossOfUse: Charged regardless of fleet utilization: the repair estimate's labor hours ÷ 4 × the daily rate on the agreement. A secondary summary adds that a stolen or salvage car is charged 15 days at the daily rate; the extracted excerpt did not show that.
enterpriseContractTerms.diminishedValue: 10% of the repair estimate when the damage is over $499
enterpriseContractTerms.other: Towing, storage and impound fees, plus the owner's costs to recover the car and establish the damage
enterpriseContractTerms.stateOverride: In states such as New York, the same jacket says the owner will not hold the renter liable for loss of use and related administrative fees.

source.publisher: Enterprise Rent-A-Car rental agreement jacket, as submitted to the Vermont Legislature (House Judiciary)
source.caveat: 2018 terms; the current jacket may differ. Claims Journal (2023-04-12) describes the same loss-of-use formula as Enterprise's method.

corroboration.note: Enterprise: labor hours ÷ 4 × daily rate. PurCo (fleet risk firm): repair days × daily rate. The column says rental cars have a higher collision rate per registered vehicle but gives no percentage.

damageFrequency.note: Neither the rental companies nor ACRISS publishes a rate of damage claims per rental. The figure 'about 10% of rentals return with damage' comes only from an unattributed search summary and is unconfirmed.

claimComposition.publisher: CarInsuRent (seller of rental excess insurance; its own customers' claims)

averageClaimReported.caveat: As printed. The collision average looks low and may be the insurer's payout rather than the rental company's bill.

source.publisher: National Law Review (press release by CarInsuRent)

JFK.note: 11.11% is the arithmetic of a 10% gross-receipts concession passed through (0.10 / 0.90). Secondary sites give both 11.11% and 11.25% for JFK. No company receipt, Hertz terms page (it returned HTTP 500) or Port Authority filing could be read. The Port Authority's JFK Schedule of Charges (Jan 2026) has no rental-car line.

sources.publisher: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey

concession.definitionCap: Enterprise-family terms define the Concession Recovery Fee as recovering airport concession fees and say it 'cannot exceed 11.11% of gross revenues'. That wording is quoted secondhand from National's fee FAQ via search and was not fetched.

airbnbAirCover.note: Airbnb publishes no average or median payout. The widely repeated 'approved claims land between $200 and $400' is a blog's estimate with no data source, so it is unconfirmed.
airbnbAirCover.frequencySource: Avada Properties, analysis of 20,000+ of its own bookings, via RapidEye Inspections. Other sites attribute the same figures to 'Safely and Guesty, 2025'. It is one property manager's data, not Airbnb's.
airbnbAirCover.claimWindow: Reimbursement requests must be filed within 14 days of checkout. AirCover pays actual cash value, not replacement cost.

sources.note: Coverage limit per search summary; page not fetched.

euroTraveller.note: The £60 figure comes from secondary reporting and search-indexed BA text. Every ba.com page, including the travel-partner fare pages, returned only a 'high demand' holding page.

longHaulEconomyStandard.note: Unconfirmed secondary claims: long-haul changes '£200+', and one source says '£100 >14 days / £500 <14 days' (that source seems to describe a different fare family or group bookings). Upgraded Points (2026-06-16) gives only a range, 'ticket change fee from $0 to $275 depending on fare type'. BA's own figure could not be read, so this is left null.

ryanair.fareDifferenceRule: The passenger pays any fare increase, and no refund is given if the new fare is lower
ryanair.note: The wording comes from the search index of ryanair.com's fees page, which renders client-side and returned only its heading. Treat it as Ryanair's own text, not yet read on the page. The fee can vary by season or route.

shareOfFlightsEmpty.what: share of European private (business aviation) flights that are empty legs
shareOfFlightsEmpty.origin: Hamilton-DLR, B. A. (2017), Economic Impact of Business Aviation in Europe (the EBAA-commissioned study), as cited by Transport & Environment
shareOfFlightsEmpty.companion: The non-empty flights carry 4.7 passengers on average

shareOfFlightsEmpty.what: share of the private-jet charter fleet that 'often flies empty'

wingX.note: WingX publishes no share of empty legs. Its glossary treats empty legs as a sector category. We found no public figure.

argusTraqpak.note: TRAQPak counts include repositioning flights, but it does not publish their share.

aviationWeek.note: We found no Aviation Week figure.

listingPractice.note: Empty legs are posted by operators and brokers (XO's 'Jet Deals', Victor, PrivateFly, Jettly, VistaJet, GlobeAir) as one-way repositioning seats or whole-aircraft sales at 25–75% off. They can be cancelled or retimed when the paying trip changes.
listingPractice.countNote: No marketplace publishes a daily count of listings. A Private Jet Card Comparisons piece (2024-09-29) quotes FlyEasy's founder saying empty legs work mostly as marketing and don't sell in volume.

ireland.note: We found no Irish operator or broker that publishes an hourly euro rate. Dublin Weston cannot take jets (turboprops and pistons only), so light jets fly from Dublin (EIDW). The nearest published European broker rates are below.

internationalFacilitiesTax2026.unit: per person per arrival or departure, for flights beginning or ending in the US (IRC §4261(c); Form 720 IRS No. 27)

us.appliesToCharter: Yes. Part 135 charter is taxable air transportation.

canada.gstHst: Zero-rated when a continuous journey's origin, destination or a stopover is outside the 'taxation area' (Canada, the continental US and St. Pierre and Miquelon). A Canada–continental US flight is not automatically zero-rated; CRA rules on transborder air apply. Charter flights sold to third-party charterers are covered in CRA GI-170.

uk.apdUnder5_7t: None. Aircraft under 5.7 tonnes MTOW are outside APD.
uk.currentHigherRate: Applies to aircraft of 20 tonnes or more with fewer than 19 seats
uk.fromApril2027: The higher rate extends to every aircraft of 5.7 tonnes or more used as a private or business jet
uk.note: Most light jets (e.g., CJ3 about 6.3 t; Phenom 300 about 8.2 t) are over 5.7 t. Only very light jets such as the Mustang (about 3.9 t) fall below. Those weights are ours and not from the source.

ireland.vat: Passenger transport outside the State is exempt with input credit, which works like zero-rating. Revenue's rate database lists passenger transport services as exempt. Ireland has no aviation ticket tax.
ireland.note: The Revenue page was found by search, but its wording for air transport was not read directly.

mexico.ivaRule: Ley del IVA art. 16: for international air transport, only 25% of the service is deemed supplied in Mexico. That 25% is taxed at 16% and the remaining 75% at 0%, so the effective rate is 4% of the fare. It applies to trips that begin in Mexico; service that begins abroad is not taxed. Flights to the 20 km border strip get the same treatment.

source.publisher: El Conta (secondary commentary on LIVA art. 16)

us.eAPIS: An APIS manifest is required for every private aircraft arriving in or departing from the US, filed through CBP's eAPIS web portal (60 minutes before departure, per CBP's private-aircraft guide).

userFeeDecal.note: Required for private aircraft; bought through DTOPS. The fee rises again on 2026-10-01; the new amount was not found. Commercial charter pays per-passenger user fees through the ticket instead.

canada.canpass: CANPASS Private Aircraft is a trusted-traveler program with a C$40 non-refundable fee per applicant 18 or over. Every person aboard must be a member, the aircraft may carry at most 15 people, and the pilot may not charge passengers, so it does not apply to a paid charter. Non-members report to CBSA's Telephone Reporting Centre before arrival and land at an airport of entry during CBSA hours.

The Enterprise damage terms (loss of use = labor hours ÷ 4 × daily rate; admin fee $50/$100/$150; diminished value 10%) come from a 2018 rental jacket. The current version was not retrieved.
JFK's 11.11% concession recovery and $4.50/day CFC are secondary. HVN's percentage was not found.
